findings.title: FY26 earnings acceleration includes a major non-operating reversal
findings.observation: Other income (expense), net moved from -$4.901 billion in FY25 to +$10.697 billion in FY26, a +$15.598 billion change. Pretax income consequently grew 34.2% and pretax margin increased 612 bps to 50.0%, while operating income grew 20.8%. Tax expense grew 47.7%, effective tax rate increased from 17.6% to 19.4%, and net income grew 31.3%.
findings.why_it_matters: The FY26 pretax and net-income acceleration was materially affected by the non-operating sign reversal and a higher tax rate. The reported P&L does not identify the composition, recurrence, or tax drivers of these items.
investigation_questions: What disclosed components comprise FY26 other income and the FY25 other expense, and what drove the sign reversal?
Which disclosed tax items or changes explain the effective tax rate increase to 19.4%?
How do the filing's operating and non-operating components reconcile to the FY26 pretax income increase?

findings.title: Service and other revenue is gaining mix while its cost intensity rises
findings.observation: Service and other revenue grew 22.7% in FY26 and had a 21.7% two-year CAGR, increasing to 80.5% of revenue from 73.6% in FY24. Product revenue was nearly flat in FY26 at +1.2% and had a -0.1% two-year CAGR, with mix declining to 19.5% from 26.4%. Service and other cost grew 26.8% and reached 28.4% of revenue, up 203 bps, while gross margin declined 88 bps to 67.9%.
findings.why_it_matters: The business mix is shifting substantially toward service and other revenue, but the associated cost line is growing faster than that revenue. Filing detail is needed to distinguish mix effects from changes within the product and service categories.
investigation_questions: What disclosed subcomponents or contract categories explain the growth in service and other revenue versus product revenue stagnation?
What drove service and other cost growth of 26.8% and its 203-bps increase in revenue intensity?
How much of the gross-margin decline reflects category mix versus margin changes within product and service categories?

findings.title: Operating expense intensity is declining and expanding operating margin
findings.observation: Against FY26 revenue growth of 17.8%, research and development grew 9.5%, sales and marketing 4.1%, and general and administrative 10.1%. Their revenue intensities declined by 82, 106, and 17 bps, respectively. Operating income grew 20.8%, and operating margin reached 46.8%, up 116 bps after a 98-bps increase in FY25.
findings.why_it_matters: Operating margin expanded despite gross-margin pressure, indicating that below-gross-profit expense intensity was an important offset. The P&L alone does not show which expense components or disclosed factors drove the improvement, including the reversal from a 5.1% G&A decline in FY25 to 10.1% growth in FY26.
investigation_questions: Which disclosed expense subcategories drove the reductions in R&D, sales and marketing, and G&A intensity?
What explains the change in G&A from -5.1% growth in FY25 to +10.1% in FY26?
How do the filing disclosures attribute the operating-margin expansion between gross profit and operating expenses?

findings.title: EPS growth largely passes through net-income growth with stable share counts
findings.observation: Basic EPS grew 31.4% in FY26 and diluted EPS grew 31.6%, closely tracking net-income growth of 31.3%. Basic average shares declined 0.1% and diluted average shares declined 0.2% in FY26; diluted shares also declined 0.1% in FY25. Basic and diluted EPS remained closely aligned in each reported period.
findings.why_it_matters: The per-share result appears primarily tied to reported net-income growth rather than a material change in average shares, but the P&L context does not explain the small basic-to-diluted difference or the share-count movements.
investigation_questions: What disclosed instruments or events explain the basic-to-diluted EPS difference in each period?
What filing disclosures explain the FY26 changes in basic and diluted weighted-average shares?
Were there any material potentially dilutive instruments affecting the diluted share calculation?
